messages:
matt.support: Heads-up: BluePeak reporting 429s from their Dedicated pool (quiet-pool-us-west-2) starting ~2026-03-10T03:40Z. Customer says spikes began right after we applied the quota migration for their plan.

emily.cs: Customer is blocked on inference for scheduled jobs, ~30% of calls failing with 429. They sent curl logs, asked for ETA to unblock. :grimacing:

nina.eng: Can you paste the API error and any quota/admin output? Trying to see if it's a runtime enforcement issue vs billing sync.

matt.support: Paste of API response they sent:```json
{"status":429,"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","detail":"quota:units_exceeded","request_id":"req_2a7b"}
```
Also ran an admin query against our tenant config:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/admin/tenants/bluepeak/quota
```
Response snippet:```json
{"tenant_id":"bluepeak","rate_units":600,"rate_denom":"minute","burst":1200}
```

arjun.platform: Wait — the billing migration intended to set rate_units=600/hour (i.e. 10 rps sustained) but this shows minute. That would increase allowed rate by 60x if minute->hour, but flipped denom could also result in 60x LOWER capacity depending on interpretation. Which direction is this?

matt.support: Looks like runtime expects denom to be "hour" for dedicated pools (we normalize to units/hour). The migration accidentally wrote the denom as "minute" for a subset of tenants, so runtime converted it to units/hour incorrectly and ended up interpreting as units/minute. Net effect: quota enforcement applied per minute instead of per hour -> customers got throttled.

sasha.sre: Confirmed in quota-cache logs on quiet-pool-us-west-2:```
2026-03-10T03:39:58Z INFO fetch_quota tenant=bluepeak rate_units=600 rate_denom=minute effective_units_per_hour=36000
2026-03-10T03:40:01Z WARN enforce_quota tenant=bluepeak tokens=600 window=60s decision=throttle
```
That looks like a denom mismatch path where our denom normalization doubled-down incorrectly in a regression.

nina.eng: Repro steps for eng: 1) Create test tenant with rate_units=600 and rate_denom=minute. 2) Send 2000 small requests over 2 minutes to dedicated pool and observe 429s after ~600. 3) Confirm enforcement logs on runtime.

arjun.platform: Quick mitigation: apply an admin override to correct denom for affected tenants and invalidate quota cache. Use admin PATCH and cache invalidation. Example:```bash
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/admin/tenants/bluepeak/quota -d '{"rate_denom":"hour"}'
# then invalidate cache
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://ops.internal/flags/quota-cache/invalidate?tenant=bluepeak
```

ops-bot: Quota cache invalidation requested by arjun.platform at 2026-03-10T04:02:12Z. JobID=qc-inv-8821.
deploy-bot: Rolling patch to billing-sync migration script scheduled (canary) - 2026-03-10T04:10Z.

emily.cs: Can we do the override now so customer can continue? They approved emergency fix.

arjun.platform: Applied patch to tenant via admin API at 2026-03-10T04:03:05Z and invalidated cache. Verified runtime logs show new fetch:```
2026-03-10T04:03:08Z INFO fetch_quota tenant=bluepeak rate_units=600 rate_denom=hour effective_units_per_hour=600
2026-03-10T04:03:09Z INFO enforce_quota tenant=bluepeak tokens=600 window=3600s decision=allow
```

matt.support: Customer confirms errors dropped from ~30% -> <1% within 2 minutes. They reran scheduled jobs and everything passed. :relieved:

sasha.sre: Root cause: migration script wrote wrong denom for subset of tenants (minute vs hour). Action items: 1) emergency override applied and validated. 2) patch migration script (canary rolling now). 3) add unit tests for denom handling in migration. 4) add monitoring alert for sudden change in denominators per-tenant.

arjun.platform: I've opened internal ticket INF-6442 to track the migration fix and tests. Also adding runbook step to do cache invalidation when changing quota fields in future.

matt.support: Leaving notes for follow-up with billing team and customer postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
